slides.title: Booster Robotics Unveils Booster T2 Humanoid Platform
slides.tldr: NEW HUMANOID PLATFORM FOR EMBODIED AI
slides.highlight: The Booster T2 humanoid platform supports embodied AI development, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated learning.

slides.title: Scaling Laws for Majority-based Opinion Dynamics in the Presence of Stubborn Agents
slides.highlight: This research analyzes how stubborn agents influence opinion distribution and steady-state convergence times in multi-agent networks, providing insights for MIMIC's societal-scale simulation of human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Analyzes how stubborn agents influence opinion consensus time in networks using a 2k-choices majority rule.
card.key_idea: Identifies a phase transition where mixing time to steady-state is exponential (sub-critical), polynomial (critical), or logarithmic (super-critical) based on stubborn agent proportions.
card.evaluation: Theoretically derived scaling laws were numerically validated by solving forward Kolmogorov and detailed balance equations for mixing times.
card.limitation: The analysis is restricted to fully connected networks and binary opinions {0, 1}.

slides.title: Mobility, Memory, and Network Structure in Agent-Based Models of Convention Tipping and Convergence
slides.highlight: This research examines how mobility, memory, and network topology influence the tipping threshold and pace of convention adoption, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation of human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: A study showing that mobility is the primary driver of convention tipping and convergence speed.
card.key_idea: An agent-based model analyzing how localized mobility, bounded memory, and network topology jointly influence the tipping threshold and time to ubiquity for binary behavioral adoption.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via 21,600 simulations across 432 configurations; a unified predictive model achieved R² = 0.91 and RMSE ≈ 57, outperforming simpler nested baselines.
card.limitation: The model is a stylized, theoretical mechanism-oriented simulation rather than an empirical predictor of specific real-world social systems.

slides.title: TRIBE: Predicting Team Performance via Communication Behavior Ensembles
slides.tldr: PREDICTING TEAM PERFORMANCE VIA COMMUNICATION PATTERNS
slides.highlight: TRIBE uses communication patterns to categorize team behavioral dynamics and predict performance, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception of hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: TRIBE predicts team performance by clustering communication patterns, enabling behavioral assessment as early as 10% task completion.
card.key_idea: A domain-independent pipeline using topic modeling (NMF/LDA) and clustering (GMM/K-means) to categorize teams into performance-predictive 'behavioral tribes' from natural language transcripts.
card.evaluation: Tested on four datasets (Minecraft, DELI, GAP); compared against Llama 3.3 and TF-IDF. Results show significant performance prediction (up to 44.3% adjusted R²).
card.limitation: Predictive strength depends on the task structure's degree of behavioral freedom; finite-answer tasks limit behavioral variation and predictive accuracy.

slides.title: Locomotion Variability and User Experience in Smart Wheelchair Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that preserving natural movement variability in shared control for smart wheelchairs increases perceived agency and usefulness. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: Preserving natural movement variability in smart wheelchair assistance improves user agency and experience without compromising performance.
card.key_idea: An autonomy-supportive shared control strategy that uses an inverted bell-shaped variability factor to reduce assistance in task-irrelevant areas while maintaining guidance at task-critical points.
card.evaluation: User study with 18 participants pushing an intelligent powered wheelchair; evaluated via ANOVA on trajectory variance, endpoint error, and subjective questionnaires (SoA, QUEAD2, UEQ).

slides.title: HUI360: A 360° Egocentric Dataset and Baselines for Human-Robot Interaction Anticipation
slides.highlight: HUI360 provides a large-scale egocentric dataset and baselines for anticipating human intentions, supporting the development of proactive and socially aware behavior in embodied agents relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: HUI360 is the largest in-the-wild 360° egocentric dataset for anticipating human-robot physical interactions.
card.key_idea: A dataset and automated pipeline for detecting, tracking, and annotating human-robot interactions using 360° videos, 2D poses, and segmentation masks to benchmark anticipation models.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using RF, MLP, and LSTM baselines on HUI360 and SSUP-A datasets. Metrics include AUC, F1-score, and Average Precision across various forecasting horizons.
card.limitation: Focuses only on physical interactions, ignoring nuanced social signals like gaze, hesitation, or verbal engagement.

slides.title: How Should I Pick a Foundation Model for My Robot? In Favor of a Community Evaluation Framework for Social Robots
slides.tldr: EVALUATION FRAMEWORK FOR SOCIAL ROBOT FOUNDATION MODELS
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a three-tiered evaluation funnel and five key dimensions to help select foundation models for social robots, supporting the RwB goal of improving human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A proposed community evaluation framework to help researchers select foundation models for embodied social robots.
card.key_idea: A three-tiered 'evaluation funnel' (static benchmarks, simulated interactions, and robot-specific tests) across five dimensions: competence, safety, character, scene effectiveness, and audience appropriateness.
card.evaluation: Proposed as a conceptual framework and case study (Haru robot); no empirical results provided, as it is a call for community development.
card.limitation: Lacks established multimodal evaluation methods and clear boundaries between simulation-based testing and live user studies.

slides.title: X2-Turn: Frame-Synchronous Dual-Head Modeling for Joint Streaming ASR and Turn State Prediction
slides.highlight: X2-Turn enables real-time distinction between user interruptions, backchannels, and utterance completion, supporting the addressee and listener modeling goals of HyECHO.

card.one_liner: X2-Turn enables joint, frame-synchronous streaming ASR and turn state prediction using a dual-head architecture.
card.key_idea: Extends Voxtral Realtime with a parallel turn state head sharing causal representations, using ASR-anchored supervision to project word-level labels onto an 80ms frame timeline.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on bilingual EasyTurn test sets against cascaded and streaming baselines; showed superior accuracy-latency trade-offs and competitive ASR performance.
card.limitation: Joint training introduces some ASR performance degradation compared to ASR-only training.

slides.title: D3D-GEN: Robot-Aware Domain-Grounded Interactive 3D World Generation for Social Robotics
slides.tldr: INTERACTIVE 3D WORLD GENERATION FOR SOCIAL ROBOTICS
slides.highlight: D3D-GEN uses a RAG pipeline to automate the creation of interactive 3D simulation environments for social navigation. This supports RwB by providing realistic, domain-grounded worlds for training and validating embodied AI.

card.one_liner: D3D-GEN generates interactive, robot-aware 3D simulation worlds grounded in autonomously retrieved domain-specific real-world knowledge.
card.key_idea: A RAG pipeline uses a domain agent to collect web-based constraints, which guide an LLM to synthesize floorplans and asset placements for simulators like Isaac Sim.
card.evaluation: Generated 450 worlds (residential, office, hospital). Compared against baselines (e.g., ProcTHOR, DiffuScene) using quantitative metrics and Gemini-based perceptual ratings; D3D-GEN showed superior scene ratings.
card.limitation: Relies on an existing 3D asset database, which may not be available for every target domain.

slides.title: High Fidelity Capture, Reconstruction, and Transfer of Human Demonstrations for Robot-Assisted Bathing
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for capturing and transferring contact-rich human bathing demonstrations to a soft robotic hand, contributing to the development of safe physical human-robot interaction relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: A framework for capturing, reconstructing, and transferring high-fidelity human bathing demonstrations to a soft-robotic hand.
card.key_idea: Uses contact regions as a processing primitive to synchronize motion, shape, and force data, enabling retargeting of clinician demonstrations to a tendon-driven soft hand.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a dataset of 128 captures (3 clinicians, 6 subjects) and real-world deployment on a mannequin using open- and closed-loop control.
card.limitation: Significant sim-to-real gap; closed-loop control uses aggregate pressure sums rather than distributions; not yet ready for human subjects.

slides.title: SAIN: Structure-Aware Interactive Navigation with Active Dialogue Grounding for Mobile Robot
slides.highlight: SAIN introduces a zero-shot framework that converts active dialogue into persistent navigation states to resolve ambiguous instructions, supporting the RwB goal of improving human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: SAIN converts active dialogue into persistent structured memories for zero-shot interactive instance goal navigation.
card.key_idea: Dialogue answers are compiled into target evidence, route-level corridor memories, and object-candidate labels, which guide frontier ranking and target approach via a unified policy.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on VL-LN IIGN benchmark; improved SR from 20.2 to 25.4 and SPL from 13.07 to 14.17 over the strongest dialogue-enabled baseline.

slides.title: TencentDB Agent Memory Launches Team Memory for Multi-Agent Collaboration
slides.highlight: The introduction of Team Memory for multi-agent collaboration is relevant to MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation using agent models.

slides.title: Robot Learning from Human Demonstrations: Handwritten Alphabet Trajectories and Human-Likeness Evaluation
slides.tldr: LEARNING HUMAN-LIKE ROBOT MOTION FROM HANDWRITING DEMONSTRATIONS
slides.highlight: This work presents a framework for learning human-like robot motion from handwriting demonstrations, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: A framework for learning human-like robot handwriting using probabilistic trajectories incorporating force and timing data.
card.key_idea: Extends GMM+GMR by adding contact force and normalized time dimensions and implementing segment-wise processing to handle multi-stroke trajectory discontinuities.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a user study (21 participants) using a simulated UR10 robot; achieved a mean human-likeness score of 71.50/100.
card.limitation: Small participant sample sizes, linear interpolation for pen-lift transitions, and lack of a pre-programmed control condition for comparison.

slides.title: X Square Robot's HOST Learns from Short Videos
slides.highlight: X Square Robot's HOST demonstrates the ability to learn from short videos, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied learning and human-robot interaction.
